title: Area and volume scale factors
keyIdea: When a shape or solid is enlarged by length scale factor k, every length is multiplied by k, every area by k² and every volume by k³. Doubling the sides of a square makes 2 × 2 = 4 copies of it; doubling the edges of a cube makes 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. This holds for any pair of similar shapes, not just squares and cubes, and for surface area as well as flat area. To go backwards, undo the power: an area factor of 25 means k = √25 = 5, and a volume factor of 27 means k = ∛27 = 3.
familyTip: Build a cube from 8 dice or sugar cubes (2 by 2 by 2). It is twice as long, wide and tall as one die but uses 8 of them, and each side shows 4 die faces: lengths × 2, area × 4, volume × 8.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: enlarge a square, a cube and a triangle, fill a jug twice as tall with small jugfuls, then find k from an area or volume factor.

kid: Enlarge a shape by scale factor k and every length is multiplied by k. Area is not. A 1 cm square enlarged by 3 becomes 3 cm by 3 cm, which holds 3 × 3 = 9 unit squares. So areas are multiplied by k².

Volume grows in three directions. A 1 cm cube enlarged by 3 becomes 3 layers of 3 by 3, which is 27 unit cubes. So volumes are multiplied by k³. Two similar jugs, one twice as tall, hold 1 and 8 jugfuls, not 1 and 2.
This works for any similar shapes, not just squares and cubes. A triangle with sides × 3 fits 9 copies of the small one. Surface area is an area, so it also goes up by k².

To work backwards, undo the power. An area factor of 25 means lengths × √25 = 5. A volume factor of 64 means lengths × ∛64 = 4. To go from areas to volumes, find k first: areas 4 : 9 give k = 3/2, so volumes are 8 : 27.
adult: Ages 15 to 17. GCSE Mathematics (DfE subject content, Higher tier G19) asks students to apply the relationships between lengths, areas and volumes in similar figures. Common Core HSG-GMD.A.3 and the Cambridge IGCSE similarity topic cover the same idea.

The reason is that area is a product of two lengths and volume of three. Scaling each length by k scales a product of two lengths by k × k and of three by k × k × k. Any area can be approximated by unit squares, and any volume by unit cubes, so the rule holds for every similar pair. Mass of a solid made of the same material scales with volume.

Common mistakes: using k for areas or volumes (a jug twice as tall holds twice as much). Using 2k instead of k² (scale factor 3 gives area × 6). Using k² for volumes. Going backwards without the root, so areas 9 : 25 are taken as lengths. Jumping from areas straight to volumes by cubing the area ratio. In the lab each slip gets a message that names it.

practice.prompt: A square is enlarged by scale factor 2. Its area is multiplied by…
practice.hint: Count the unit squares in a 2 by 2 square.
practice.explain: 2 × 2 = 4 unit squares fill the enlarged square, so the area is multiplied by 2² = 4.

practice.prompt: A shape has area 5 cm². It is enlarged by scale factor {k}. What is the new area in cm²?
practice.hint: Area factor = k², so multiply by {k} × {k}.

practice.prompt: A solid has volume 3 cm³. It is enlarged by scale factor {k}. What is the new volume in cm³?
practice.hint: Volume grows in three directions, so the volume factor is k³ (k × k × k).

practice.prompt: Two similar solids have volumes in the ratio 1 : 27. What is the ratio of their lengths?
practice.hint: Volume factor = k³. Undo the cube.
practice.explain: ∛27 = 3, so the lengths are in the ratio 1 : 3. 1 : 9 would be the area ratio.

practice.prompt: Two similar jugs: the big one is twice as tall. How many small jugfuls fill it?
practice.hint: Every length doubles, including width and depth.
practice.explain: Volume factor 2³ = 8, so 8 small jugfuls fill it. 2 uses only the height, and 4 forgets the depth.

pool.prompt: A photo is enlarged by scale factor 3. Its area is multiplied by…
pool.explain: 3 × 3 = 9. Using 6 doubles the factor instead of squaring it.

pool.prompt: Similar cylinders: the big one is {k} times as tall as the small one. The small one holds 10 cm³. How many cm³ does the big one hold?
Two similar shapes have areas in the ratio 1 : {=k*k}. The small one has a side of 4 cm. How long is the matching side of the big one, in cm?
Similar solids have surface areas 9 cm² and 25 cm². What is the ratio of their lengths?
pool.hint: Surface area is an area. Undo the square.

pool.prompt: Similar cones have volumes in the ratio 8 : 125. What is the ratio of their surface areas?
pool.hint: Find the length ratio first, then square it.

pool.prompt: A model car is 1/20 of full size. How many times as much paint does the real car need?
pool.hint: Paint covers a surface. Is that a length, an area or a volume?
pool.explain: Paint covers an area, so the factor is 20² = 400. 8000 = 20³ would be for volume.

pool.prompt: A cube's edges are halved. What happens to its volume?
pool.hint: Half the height means k = 1/2. Volume uses k³, so cube the half.
pool.explain: (1/2)³ = 1/8, so the volume becomes one eighth. 1/4 is what happens to each face's area.

pool.prompt: A solid metal statue is enlarged by scale factor 2, using the same metal. The small one has a mass of 3 kg. What is the mass of the big one in kg?
pool.hint: Mass depends on volume when the material is the same.
pool.explain: Volume factor 2³ = 8, so the mass is 3 × 8 = 24 kg.
